title: What makes love last? With Arthur Aron, PhD

sentences.en: If you have ever fallen in love, you probably remember the intensity of the longing and desire that you felt for the object of your affection.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经坠入爱河，你可能还记得那种对心上人强烈的渴望与思念。

sentences.en: The breathless anticipation of seeing each other wanting the moments together to last forever.
sentences.zh: 那种见到彼此的屏息期待，以及希望共处的时光能永恒延续的愿望。

sentences.en: For most of us, that passionate intensity fades over time.
sentences.zh: 对我们大多数人来说，那种炽热的激情会随着时间推移而消退。

sentences.en: Few people celebrate their 10th or 20th Valentine's Day together with the same enthusiasm that they did their firSt.
sentences.zh: 很少有人能像第一次过情人节那样，怀着同样的热情去庆祝第 10 个或第 20 个情人节。

sentences.en: But some couples remain deeply and passionately in love even after decades of marriage.
sentences.zh: 但有些伴侣即使在结婚几十年后，依然深爱着对方，充满激情。

sentences.en: What is it that sets those relationships apart?
sentences.zh: 是什么让这些关系与众不同呢？

sentences.en: What makes love like that last?
sentences.zh: 是什么让这样的爱情能够持久？

sentences.en: Are some couples just lucky or are there things that any couple can do to sustain love or rekindle it in a long-term relationship?
sentences.zh: 是有些伴侣运气好，还是说任何伴侣都能采取一些行动来维持或重燃长期关系中的爱意？

sentences.en: What does science say about the secrets of everlasting love?
sentences.zh: 科学对于永恒爱情的秘密有何见解？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是 Kim Mills。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Arthur Aron, a professor of psychology at Stony Brook University in New York.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是纽约石溪大学的心理学教授 Arthur Aron 博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Aron has spent decades studying how people develop and maintain close relationships, particularly romantic relationships.
sentences.zh: Aron 博士花费数十年研究人们如何建立和维持亲密关系，尤其是浪漫关系。

sentences.en: He developed the self-expansion model of relationships, which posits that one main motivation for forming bonds with others is our own personal growth.
sentences.zh: 他提出了关系的“自我扩展模型”，该模型认为，与他人建立联系的主要动机之一是我们自身的个人成长。

sentences.en: Relationships allow us to grow and expand our sense of self.
sentences.zh: 关系让我们能够成长并扩展我们的自我意识。

sentences.en: Outside of academia, Dr. Aron is perhaps best known for developing the 36 questions that lead to love,
sentences.zh: 在学术界之外，Aron 博士最出名的或许是他开发的“通往爱情的 36 个问题”，

sentences.en: work that was profiled in a New York Times modern love column that went viral a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 这项研究几年前在《纽约时报》的“现代爱情”专栏中被报道，并迅速走红。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us, Dr. Aron.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目，Aron 博士。

sentences.en: My pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: Let's start with the big question I posed in the introduction.
sentences.zh: 让我们从我在引言中提出的那个大问题开始吧。

sentences.en: What makes love last?
sentences.zh: 是什么让爱情持久？

sentences.en: You've done research on couples who say they're still madly in love after many years together.
sentences.zh: 您曾对那些结婚多年后仍声称深爱着对方的伴侣进行过研究。

sentences.en: How do they do it?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Let me just say a word about the fact that it really can happen.
sentences.zh: 首先，我想说，这种情况确实可能发生。

sentences.en: We have a lot of studies showing that.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多研究都证明了这一点。

sentences.en: People find it hard to believe it really can happen.
sentences.zh: 人们很难相信这真的会发生。

sentences.en: For example, in a representative U.S.
sentences.zh: 例如，在几年前我们进行的一项美国代表性调查中，

sentences.en: survey we did a few years ago, of people married 10 years or longer, 40% claim to be very intensely in love.
sentences.zh: 针对结婚 10 年或以上的人群，40% 的人声称自己依然深陷爱河。

sentences.en: And that was on a seven-point scale where five was somewhat in love, six is a little in love.
sentences.zh: 那是在一个七分量表上，5 分代表“有点爱”，6 分代表“有一点爱”。

sentences.en: You know, those are the low end.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些是低分段。

sentences.en: But intensely in love, very in love.
sentences.zh: 但“深陷爱河”、“非常爱”，

sentences.en: This is even higher than that.
sentences.zh: 这比那个分数还要高。

sentences.en: Very intensely in love.
sentences.zh: 是非常深地坠入爱河。

sentences.en: And if you look at people who were married greater than 30 years, we still had almost that many.
sentences.zh: 如果你观察那些结婚超过 30 年的人，我们发现比例依然差不多。

sentences.en: 40% of women, 35% of men.
sentences.zh: 40% 的女性，35% 的男性。

sentences.en: Now, of course, that's the people who are still together.
sentences.zh: 当然，这指的是那些依然在一起的人。

sentences.en: So it means if you get married and only half are still together 10 years later, 20%.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着如果你结婚了，只有一半人在 10 年后还在一起，那就是 20%。

sentences.en: But still, that's a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，这依然是很大一部分人。

sentences.en: And we were concerned whether this is really the case or they're just saying so.
sentences.zh: 我们当时很担心这是否真的是事实，还是他们只是随口说说。

sentences.en: And so we did some fMRI studies, some brain scan studies.
sentences.zh: 所以我们做了一些功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）研究，也就是脑部扫描研究。

sentences.en: Now, I've done with my colleagues a lot of studies of people who are newly in love.
sentences.zh: 我和同事们做过很多关于新婚燕尔人群的研究。

sentences.en: So we know what the brain looks like, particularly something called the dopamine reward area.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道大脑是什么样子，特别是所谓的“多巴胺奖励区域”。

sentences.en: Responds when you see it, you've fallen in love.
sentences.zh: 当你看到心上人时，它会做出反应，说明你坠入爱河了。

sentences.en: So we recruited people who claimed to be, we went around in New York and we recruited people who said
sentences.zh: 所以我们在纽约招募了那些声称自己依然深爱伴侣的人，

sentences.en: whether they were still madly in love with their partner, who were married at least 10 years.
sentences.zh: 他们结婚至少 10 年了。

sentences.en: On the average, the sample we studied was married 20 years.
sentences.zh: 平均而言，我们研究的样本结婚了 20 年。

sentences.en: And they were really, they claimed to be intensely in love.
sentences.zh: 他们确实声称自己深陷爱河。

sentences.en: We interviewed them.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了他们。

sentences.en: They looked like it.
sentences.zh: 他们看起来确实如此。

sentences.en: One, my then graduate student, now a very successful professor, researcher, Bianca Acevedo, told me about one couple she interviewed and she could see it.
sentences.zh: 我当时的一位研究生，现在已经是一位非常成功的教授和研究员，Bianca Acevedo，曾告诉我她采访过的一对伴侣，她能看出来。

sentences.en: They were saying, you know, when we talk to our friends, these are people who are in their 60s.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你知道，当我们和朋友交谈时——这些人已经 60 多岁了——

sentences.en: When we talk to our friends, they're always complaining because we're always all over each other physically.
sentences.zh: 当我们和朋友聊天时，他们总是在抱怨，因为我们总是黏在一起。

sentences.en: So when we looked at their brains, when we did the same basic brain scan, what happens when you see your partner versus a familiar other who's equally attractive,
sentences.zh: 所以当我们观察他们的大脑时，当我们进行同样的脑部扫描，观察当你看到伴侣与看到同样有吸引力的熟人时，

sentences.en: what we see is that same activation as much as the people who've newly fallen in love.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是与那些刚坠入爱河的人一样的大脑激活。

sentences.en: There were some minor differences.
sentences.zh: 有一些细微的差别。

sentences.en: They didn't show the anxiety that we see in people who've just fallen in love.
sentences.zh: 他们没有表现出我们在刚坠入爱河的人身上看到的焦虑。

sentences.en: And they did show activation in what's called the pair bonding area, which we see in animals.
sentences.zh: 而且他们确实在所谓的“配对结合区域”表现出了激活，我们在动物身上也观察到这一点。

sentences.en: But it does seem like it really can happen.
sentences.zh: 但这看起来确实是可能发生的。

sentences.en: Now, not everyone's happy to hear this because if you're planning to get married, it sounds good.
sentences.zh: 现在，并不是每个人都乐于听到这个消息，因为如果你正打算结婚，这听起来不错。

sentences.en: But one of the ways people feel good about their relationships is by comparing to other relationships.
sentences.zh: 但人们对自己的关系感到满意的方式之一，就是通过与他人的关系进行比较。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, it should be a motivation to do something.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，这应该成为采取行动的动力。

sentences.en: Are there characteristics that these madly in love couples tend to share?
sentences.zh: 这些深陷爱河的伴侣是否有共同的特征？

sentences.en: Do they meet at older or younger ages?
sentences.zh: 他们是在较年长还是较年轻时相遇的？

sentences.en: Does that matter?
sentences.zh: 这重要吗？

sentences.en: Do they have certain types of personalities?
sentences.zh: 他们是否有某种特定的人格？

sentences.en: Are they very similar in their outlooks on life?
sentences.zh: 他们对生活的看法非常相似吗？

sentences.en: Or are they opposites who attracted?
sentences.zh: 还是说异性相吸？

sentences.en: Well, as far as initial attraction, that doesn't seem to affect things as much years later.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就最初的吸引力而言，这似乎对多年后的关系影响不大。

sentences.en: Now, who you are and who your partner is do matter a lot.
sentences.zh: 现在，你是谁以及你的伴侣是谁确实很重要。

sentences.en: And your skills matter a lot.
sentences.zh: 而且你们的技能也非常重要。

sentences.en: And, you know, people think similarity is very important.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，人们认为相似性非常重要。

sentences.en: And it turns out it's, I mean, it's important to share values, but it's not so important to share personality.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，分享价值观很重要，但分享人格并不是那么重要。

sentences.en: You know, if one of you gets angry easy, it's not better if both of you get angry easily.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你们中有一个人容易生气，那么两个人都容易生气并不会更好。

sentences.en: But we like to think we're similar on all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 但我们喜欢认为我们在各方面都很相似。

sentences.en: And, of course, as people are longer together, they become more similar, not just in their ideas, but in their physical appearance.
sentences.zh: 当然，随着人们在一起的时间越长，他们会变得越相似，不仅是在思想上，在身体外貌上也是如此。

sentences.en: People tend to look more alike over time.
sentences.zh: 人们往往会随着时间的推移看起来越来越像。

sentences.en: Anyway, I won't go into that sidestep.
sentences.zh: 总之，我就不偏离主题了。

sentences.en: You can measure that.
sentences.zh: 你可以测量这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, it's for real.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是真的。

sentences.en: People always say that.
sentences.zh: 人们总是这么说。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: There's been some wonderful studies done where they've shown people pictures of individuals taken when they were getting married.
sentences.zh: 有一些很棒的研究，他们向人们展示了个人结婚时拍的照片。

sentences.en: And then they showed people pictures of who they are now.
sentences.zh: 然后他们向人们展示了他们现在的照片。

sentences.en: And they had, you know, many different people they showed them.
sentences.zh: 他们展示给了许多不同的人看。

sentences.en: But people right away saw much more similarity.
sentences.zh: 但人们一眼就看出了更多的相似之处。

sentences.en: So what can people do to make this happen?
sentences.zh: 那么人们能做些什么来促成这一点呢？

sentences.en: And we know quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 我们知道得相当多。

sentences.en: We don't know everything, but we know quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 我们虽然不知道一切，但知道得相当多。

sentences.en: And you can help make it happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以帮助实现这一点。

sentences.en: There are certain things that are sort of essential to make it basically okay.
sentences.zh: 有些事情是让关系基本顺畅的必要条件。

sentences.en: And those are crucial because if it's not basically okay, it's hard to sparkle.
sentences.zh: 这些至关重要，因为如果关系本身不顺畅，就很难焕发光彩。

sentences.en: And there are people who are intensely in love that aren't happy, but not many.
sentences.zh: 有些深陷爱河的人并不快乐，但不多。

sentences.en: Usually, if your partner's responding and you're, you know, Chelsea in love, you're very happy.
sentences.zh: 通常，如果你的伴侣有回应，而你又深陷爱河，你会非常快乐。

sentences.en: So there are basically four basic things that are sort of crucial to make a relationship at least okay.
sentences.zh: 所以，让一段关系至少保持顺畅，基本上有四个关键点。

sentences.en: I mean, sometimes they'll manage without them, but they really make a difference.
sentences.zh: 我是说，有时没有它们也能维持，但它们确实能带来不同。

sentences.en: One of the biggest is another one people don't want to hear, and that is yourself.
sentences.zh: 其中最重要的一点是人们不想听到的，那就是你自己。

sentences.en: If you're anxious or depressed or insecure, it's very hard to feel happy in your relationship.
sentences.zh: 如果你焦虑、抑郁或缺乏安全感，就很难在关系中感到快乐。

sentences.en: Initially, you might be, but then you sort of start blaming it on the other person or, you know, you just go back to being unhappy.
sentences.zh: 起初你可能会，但随后你开始将其归咎于对方，或者，你知道，你只是回到了不快乐的状态。

sentences.en: So one of the biggest things you can do is to get therapy, or if it's not very big, learn to meditate.
sentences.zh: 所以你能做的最重要的事情之一就是接受治疗，或者如果问题不大，学习冥想。

sentences.en: Or if it's very big, you know, see a psychiatrist, get medication.
sentences.zh: 或者如果问题很大，你知道，去看精神科医生，进行药物治疗。

sentences.en: You know, if you're insecure, that's another big factor.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你缺乏安全感，那是另一个重要因素。

sentences.en: There are some things you can do.
sentences.zh: 你可以做一些事情。

sentences.en: People with low self-esteem have a hard time.
sentences.zh: 自尊心低的人会过得很艰难。

sentences.en: Some great work by Murray and Holmes and others.
sentences.zh: Murray 和 Holmes 等人做了一些出色的研究。

sentences.en: If you have low self-esteem, it's hard to feel, you know, your partner likes you.
sentences.zh: 如果你自尊心低，就很难感受到伴侣喜欢你。

sentences.en: There's that old joke of Groucho Marx.
sentences.zh: 这就是 Groucho Marx 的那个老笑话。

sentences.en: I wouldn't belong to any club that would have me as a member.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会加入任何愿意接纳我为会员的俱乐部。

sentences.en: So, you know, you wonder, you know, if your partner, what's wrong with your partner if they like you?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你会怀疑，如果你的伴侣喜欢你，那他们是不是有什么问题？

sentences.en: Or could your partner really like you?
sentences.zh: 或者你的伴侣真的能喜欢你吗？

sentences.en: So, some nice research has been done showing that one of the things you can do is to think if your partner compliments you, you know, try to think about it abstractly.
sentences.zh: 所以，一些不错的研究表明，你可以做的一件事是，如果你的伴侣赞美你，试着抽象地去思考它。

sentences.en: Try to look at sort of why your partner said it and what it means to you.
sentences.zh: 试着去看看为什么你的伴侣会这么说，以及这对你意味着什么。

sentences.en: Of course, who your partner is matters too.
sentences.zh: 当然，你的伴侣是谁也很重要。

sentences.en: But it matters even more who you are.
sentences.zh: 但你是谁更重要。

sentences.en: And then another one, a huge one, is stress.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个巨大的因素，就是压力。

sentences.en: If you're under great stress or some big thing happens in your life, you know, one of you loses a job or worse yet, a child dies, you know, those are really hard.
sentences.zh: 如果你承受着巨大的压力，或者生活中发生了什么大事，比如你们中一人失业，或者更糟的是，孩子去世了，这些真的很难。

sentences.en: And they're not only hard because they affect you.
sentences.zh: 它们不仅因为影响你而变得困难。

sentences.en: So, when you're under stress, you don't behave as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你承受压力时，你的表现就不会那么好。

sentences.en: And you're likely to, you know, if your partner does one little thing, you may just go off the top.
sentences.zh: 而且你很可能会，如果你的伴侣做了一件小事，你可能会立刻爆发。

sentences.en: You know, you can't see, oh, well, they weren't usually like that.
sentences.zh: 你无法看到，哦，他们平时不是那样的。

sentences.en: And if your partner does it, it's hard to remember that, you know, they're under stress if they're also under stress.
sentences.zh: 如果你的伴侣也承受着压力，就很难记住他们也是在压力之下。

sentences.en: So, it's important when you're under stress to try to remember this effect that stress can have.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你有压力时，试着记住压力可能产生的这种影响是很重要的。

sentences.en: Because your ability to think broadly is hard.
sentences.zh: 因为你全面思考的能力会受到限制。

sentences.en: But if you can remember that one thing, it can help in interpreting yourself and your partner's behavior.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能记住这一点，它有助于解读你自己和伴侣的行为。

sentences.en: And more generally, communication skills is a huge factor.
sentences.zh: 更广泛地说，沟通技巧是一个巨大的因素。

sentences.en: Your partner and you need to feel you're hearing each other.
sentences.zh: 你和你的伴侣需要感受到你们在倾听彼此。

sentences.en: That's what's called responsiveness.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的“回应性”。

sentences.en: Harry Reese, a great social psychologist in this field, he and many of his colleagues have shown that one of the biggest things in interacting with people,
sentences.zh: Harry Reese，这个领域的一位伟大的社会心理学家，他和他的许多同事已经证明，在与人互动时，

sentences.en: especially close others, is feeling that they're responsive to you.
sentences.zh: 尤其是与亲密的人互动时，最重要的事情之一就是感受到他们对你有回应。

sentences.en: They hear you.
sentences.zh: 他们听到了你的声音。

sentences.en: They understand you.
sentences.zh: 他们理解你。

sentences.en: They, you know, they verify what you say.
sentences.zh: 他们验证了你说的话。

sentences.en: They care about you.
sentences.zh: 他们关心你。

sentences.en: And so, you want to show that to your partner and you want to reveal things about yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以，你想向你的伴侣展示这一点，你也想向对方展示真实的自己。

sentences.en: We'll talk more about the 36th questions later, but that's a little what that's about.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会更多地讨论那 36 个问题，但这就是它的意义所在。

sentences.en: You want to reveal a little to give the other opportunity to be responsive.
sentences.zh: 你想透露一点自己，给对方一个做出回应的机会。

sentences.en: And you want to be responsive to your partner.
sentences.zh: 而且你想对你的伴侣做出回应。

sentences.en: And then, of course, there's handling conflict, which is a huge problem.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有处理冲突，这是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: I was going to ask that one.
sentences.zh: 我正想问这个问题。

sentences.en: That's a big one.
sentences.zh: 那是一个大问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And conflict's kind of inevitable in relationships, but it isn't always, you know, rising.
sentences.zh: 冲突在关系中是不可避免的，但它并不总是会升级。

sentences.en: But one of the recent lines of research on that has shown that when you're in a conflict, try to think about it from a third person's perspective, who is neutral.
sentences.zh: 但最近关于这一点的一项研究表明，当你们发生冲突时，试着从一个中立的第三方的角度去思考。

sentences.en: But they care about your relationship, but they're not on either side.
sentences.zh: 他们关心你们的关系，但他们不偏袒任何一方。

sentences.en: Try to see if you can reflect it from that perspective.
sentences.zh: 试着看看你是否能从那个角度去反思。

sentences.en: And then there's some sort of rules you should follow.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有一些你应该遵循的规则。

sentences.en: John Gottman's done all this wonderful research.
sentences.zh: 约翰·戈特曼（John Gottman）做过所有这些出色的研究。

sentences.en: He calls them the four horsemen of the apocalypse.
sentences.zh: 他称之为“末日四骑士”。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Things you should avoid, you know, criticism, defensiveness, contempt, stonewalling, you know, what he calls kitchen sinking.
sentences.zh: 你应该避免的事情，你知道，比如批评、辩解、蔑视、筑墙，还有他所说的“翻旧账”。

sentences.en: You know, the person does one thing and you remind them of everything that's always annoyed you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对方做了一件事，你就把所有让你心烦的事都翻出来提醒他们。

sentences.en: You don't want to do that.
sentences.zh: 你可不想那样做。

sentences.en: In fact, you should sort of sometimes discuss this with your partner when you're not in a conflict so that you have some sort of rules.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你应该在没有冲突的时候和伴侣讨论这些，这样你们就能制定一些规则。

sentences.en: And another thing is, if you're really worked up, I mean, in a negative way or angry or upset, it's not so good to discuss it.
sentences.zh: 还有一点，如果你情绪非常激动，我是说，以一种消极的方式，或者感到愤怒或沮丧时，讨论这些问题并不好。

sentences.en: You know, if your pulse is over 100, the thing to do is to go, you know, say to your partner, I'm not leaving you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你的脉搏超过100次，你应该做的是，你知道，对你的伴侣说，我不是要离开你。

sentences.en: I'm not, you know, just stopping talking about it, but I should have 20 minutes to settle down.
sentences.zh: 我不是，你知道，只是不想再谈论这件事了，但我需要20分钟冷静一下。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then you go back to the discussion.
sentences.zh: 然后再回到讨论中来。

sentences.en: You don't want to just leave it.
sentences.zh: 你不能就这么搁置不管。

sentences.en: Anyway, those are some things for handling conflict that we know.
sentences.zh: 总之，这些是我们所知的处理冲突的一些方法。

sentences.en: So it's not my main area of expertise, but it's really important.
sentences.zh: 这不是我的主要研究领域，但它确实非常重要。

sentences.en: And then there's one other thing, and that is family and friends, if they disapprove.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事，那就是如果家人和朋友不赞成你们的关系。

sentences.en: The iconic example of love in the West is what?
sentences.zh: 西方爱情的标志性例子是什么？

sentences.en: The iconic example of love.
sentences.zh: 爱情的标志性例子。

sentences.en: In literature in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 在西方的文学作品中。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, you know, there's always Romeo and Juliet.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，你知道，总有罗密欧与朱丽叶。

sentences.en: And of course, there was family conflict.
sentences.zh: 当然，那里面有家庭冲突。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: How did that work out?
sentences.zh: 结果如何呢？

sentences.en: Not so well.
sentences.zh: 不太好。

sentences.en: Yeah, they were intensely in love.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们爱得非常深沉。

sentences.en: But no, if your family, you know, this isn't as big a problem for most Westerners, but in many cultures and many people who are from other cultures,
sentences.zh: 但不是，如果你的家人，你知道，这对大多数西方人来说不是什么大问题，但在许多文化中，以及许多来自其他文化的人来说，

sentences.en: what your family thinks matters a lot.
sentences.zh: 你家人的想法非常重要。

sentences.en: In the short run, sometimes it makes you feel better if your parents disapprove, if you're an American.
sentences.zh: 短期来看，如果你是美国人，父母的不赞成有时反而会让你感觉更好。

sentences.en: But in the long run, it's hard, especially once you start having children and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，这很困难，尤其是当你开始有孩子之类的事情之后。

sentences.en: So you really want to work.
sentences.zh: 所以你真的需要努力。

sentences.en: And of course, if your friends strongly disapprove, you really want to work to create good relationships.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你的朋友强烈反对，你真的需要努力去建立良好的关系。

sentences.en: So those are some things that are sort of essential.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都是一些至关重要的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, essential is a little too strong because there are people who somehow manage, you know, if just one of these things is in place, if the other three are out.
sentences.zh: 我是说，说“至关重要”有点太绝对了，因为有些人即使只有其中一件事到位，其他三样缺失，也能设法维持。

sentences.en: But it's a lot harder.
sentences.zh: 但这要困难得多。

sentences.en: And so these are things you want to do to get it to the level where, you know, it's at least okay.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是你想要做的事情，为了让关系达到一个，你知道，至少还不错的水平。

sentences.en: So what advice would you give to our listeners who, you know, feel inspired by what you're saying and they want to improve their relationships?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于那些受到你所说的话启发，想要改善关系的听众，你会给他们什么建议呢？

sentences.en: So what can they do to take a relationship that's maybe okay or maybe it's gotten a little boring?
sentences.zh: 他们能做些什么来改善一段可能还凑合，或者可能变得有点无聊的关系呢？

sentences.en: How can they rekindle the intense love that they felt at the beginning?
sentences.zh: 他们如何才能重燃起初感受到的那种强烈的爱？

sentences.en: Well, there's a few crucial things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有几件关键的事情。

sentences.en: One is, of course, creating time together by yourself, particularly if you have kids, you know, or you're living with an extended family.
sentences.zh: 第一，当然是创造你们独处的时间，特别是如果你有孩子，你知道，或者你和大家庭住在一起。

sentences.en: You need to have some time by yourself with your partner.
sentences.zh: 你需要和你的伴侣有一些独处的时间。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, you need to have some time together.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，你们需要有一些在一起的时间。

sentences.en: Of course, right now during the pandemic, you mentioned a little time apart, too.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在疫情期间，你也提到了需要一点分开的时间。

sentences.en: A little too much time.
sentences.zh: 时间有点太多了。

sentences.en: Yeah, but the thing is to sort of pull yourself out of this environment and just working and this and that and really have some time to get.
sentences.zh: 是的，但关键是要把自己从这种环境中抽离出来，不仅仅是工作，这那的，真正花点时间在一起。

sentences.en: And then how you use that time is kind of crucial.
sentences.zh: 然后，你如何利用这段时间至关重要。

sentences.en: You know, being playful is really, you know, really important.
sentences.zh: 你知道，保持爱玩的心态真的，你知道，非常重要。

sentences.en: And particularly my research on self-expansion is really central.
sentences.zh: 特别是我的关于“自我扩展”的研究，这真的很核心。

sentences.en: Doing things that are new and interesting with your partner matters hugely.
sentences.zh: 和你的伴侣一起做一些新鲜有趣的事情非常重要。

sentences.en: You know, not just same old, same old, but new, different.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不要总是老一套，要新鲜、不同。

sentences.en: So what might those things be if you're talking about self-expansion?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果谈到“自我扩展”，这些事情可能是什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, it could be, you know, at one level it could be flying, you know, in a helicopter together.
sentences.zh: 嗯，可能是，你知道，从某种程度上说，可能是两人一起坐直升机飞行。

sentences.en: But it could also just be taking a cooking class together or, you know, doing something new and interesting.
sentences.zh: 但也可能只是两人一起去上烹饪课，或者，你知道，做一些新鲜有趣的事情。

sentences.en: And it could be a little thing or a big thing.
sentences.zh: 可以是小事，也可以是大事。

sentences.en: My wife and I, you know, we went kayaking, you know, down the river and that was lovely on our own.
sentences.zh: 我和我妻子，你知道，我们去划皮划艇，你知道，顺流而下，那真的很棒，就我们俩。

sentences.en: It wasn't dangerous.
sentences.zh: 那并不危险。

sentences.en: We picked a river that wasn't dangerous, just the fun of it.
sentences.zh: 我们选了一条不危险的河流，纯粹是为了好玩。

sentences.en: It's a little challenging, but that makes it all the better.
sentences.zh: 这有点挑战性，但这让它变得更好。

sentences.en: Or another example is one night we were coming home or coming back from a play and we walked by a bar.
sentences.zh: 或者另一个例子是，有一天晚上我们看完戏回家，路过一家酒吧。

sentences.en: He said, we haven't hung out in a bar in years and years.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们已经好多年没去过酒吧了。

sentences.en: So we went and hung out in a bar for a little while.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就进去坐了一会儿。

sentences.en: So, you know, in one of our studies, one of our first studies, we had a large sample of couples agreed to be in the study.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在我们的一项研究中，我们最初的研究之一，我们让一大批同意参加研究的夫妇参与进来。

sentences.en: And we asked them, we gave them a big list of activities couples do together.
sentences.zh: 我们给了他们一份很长的清单，列出了夫妇们可以一起做的活动。

sentences.en: And we said, you know, for each one separately, we said, how exciting would this be to do with your partner and how pleasant would it be?
sentences.zh: 我们对他们说，你知道，对每一项分别评价，我们问，和你的伴侣一起做这件事会有多令人兴奋，会有多愉快？

sentences.en: And then we gave them a list that was based on what both of them is rated as highly pleasant, but only moderately exciting.
sentences.zh: 然后我们给他们一份清单，是基于他们两人都评价为“非常愉快”但“兴奋度一般”的活动。

sentences.en: And another and another half were randomly assigned to get a list that was highly exciting, but not not rated as high unpleasantness, not low unpleasantness.
sentences.zh: 另一半人被随机分配到一份清单，上面是“非常令人兴奋”但“愉快度评价不高”的活动。

sentences.en: And we asked them to do something for about an hour every week from the list we gave them.
sentences.zh: 我们要求他们每周从我们给的清单中选一件事情做，大约一个小时。

sentences.en: And then after 10 weeks, the couples that had done from the exciting list were substantially increased in their satisfaction with their relationship.
sentences.zh: 10周后，那些做了“令人兴奋”清单上活动的夫妇，对关系的满意度有了显著提高。

sentences.en: In fact, the other couples were slightly less so, but not much so.
sentences.zh: 事实上，另一组夫妇的满意度略有下降，但幅度不大。

sentences.en: You know, it's also boredom is a problem.
sentences.zh: 你知道，无聊也是个问题。

sentences.en: You know, we've done lab studies.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们做过实验室研究。

sentences.en: We had a study where people came into, couples came into the lab and they were told they'd be videotaped doing an activity together.
sentences.zh: 我们有一项研究，夫妇们来到实验室，被告知他们一起做活动时会被录像。

sentences.en: And they filled out some questionnaires firSt.
sentences.zh: 他们先填写了一些问卷。

sentences.en: And we did take them, but it didn't matter what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 我们确实录了，但他们做什么并不重要。

sentences.en: We, in one condition, the expanding condition, we tied their wrists and ankles together with Velcro straps.
sentences.zh: 我们，在一种情况下，即“扩展”条件下，我们用魔术贴带子把他们的手腕和脚踝绑在一起。

sentences.en: And they had a big, long gym mat, you know, that went very long, two or three of them across the room.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个又大又长的健身垫，你知道，很长，两三个垫子铺满整个房间。

sentences.en: They had to push a foam roller across and back without using their fingers or teeth and over a barrier in the middle, a round barrier.
sentences.zh: 他们必须在不使用手指或牙齿的情况下，把一个泡沫滚轴推过去再推回来，还要越过中间的一个障碍物，一个圆形的障碍物。

sentences.en: And they had to do it within a certain amount of time.
sentences.zh: 他们必须在一定时间内完成。

sentences.en: And they had three chances to do it, four chances to do it.
sentences.zh: 他们有三次机会，四次机会来完成。

sentences.en: Sounds like a TV show, you know, like beat the clock.
sentences.zh: 听起来像个电视节目，你知道，像《挑战时间》之类的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the control condition, they just each went back separately and it was pleasant.
sentences.zh: 在对照组中，他们只是各自回去，这很愉快。

sentences.en: They didn't mind that.
sentences.zh: 他们不介意这一点。

sentences.en: They thought it was sort of funny, but they didn't know about the other condition.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得这挺有趣的，但他们不知道还有另一种情况。

sentences.en: And then, and we, we timed it.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们，我们计时了。

sentences.en: They had, you know, they had to take watches off to do this and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们有，你知道，他们得摘下手表来做这个之类的。

sentences.en: So we timed it so that they didn't quite make it the first two times.
sentences.zh: 所以我们计时，让他们前两次刚好没完成。

sentences.en: The third time they just made, if it was unbelievable that they had made it the third time, then they made it the fourth time.
sentences.zh: 第三次他们刚好完成了，如果第三次完成简直不可思议，然后他们第四次也完成了。

sentences.en: And the couples who did the exciting activity versus the pleasant.
sentences.zh: 那些做“令人兴奋”活动的夫妇对比那些做“愉快”活动的夫妇。

sentences.en: Well, we had in one of the, in a couple of the studies, we had a questionnaire afterwards, but in another study, we had them have a conversation afterwards.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在其中几项研究中，我们事后有问卷调查，但在另一项研究中，我们让他们事后进行了一次谈话。

sentences.en: And again, they didn't know which condition they were in or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 同样，他们不知道自己处于哪种条件下，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And the conversation was, you know, it was friendly conversation.
sentences.zh: 谈话是，你知道，友好的谈话。

sentences.en: Suppose you were given a bunch of money to go on a trip, where would you choose to go or to remodel your home, you know?
sentences.zh: 假设给你一笔钱去旅行，你会选择去哪里，或者去装修你的房子，你知道？

sentences.en: And we had people coding the conversations who didn't know which condition the subjects were in.
sentences.zh: 我们让那些不知道受试者处于哪种条件下的编码员来分析这些谈话。

sentences.en: And those who were in the exciting condition have much more positive interaction.
sentences.zh: 处于“令人兴奋”条件下的那些人，互动要积极得多。

sentences.en: And then there's been studies that, by others, I mean, there's been a lot of replication of this, studies that followed people up four months later, you know, things like that.
sentences.zh: 还有其他人做的研究，我是说，这已经有很多重复验证了，比如四个月后回访人们的研究，诸如此类。

sentences.en: We did one study where we had a sample that had been, this is from Terry Orbach and group sample, where they had a large sample, national sample.
sentences.zh: 我们做过一项研究，样本是，这是来自Terry Orbach团队的样本，他们有一个很大的全国性样本。

sentences.en: And they followed people for like, what was that?
sentences.zh: 他们追踪了人们，比如，那是多久？

sentences.en: I think it was year nine and 17, something like that we were looking at.
sentences.zh: 我想是第9年和第17年，大概是我们在看的那些时间点。

sentences.en: And their ratings of how exciting their daily life is with their partner, how bored they were, you know, predicted their satisfaction at year 17, you know, nine years later,
sentences.zh: 他们对与伴侣的日常生活有多令人兴奋、有多无聊的评价，预测了他们在第17年的满意度，你知道，九年后，

sentences.en: whatever it was.
sentences.zh: 无论那是多久。

sentences.en: And some of the most recent research has shown that one of the reasons this is working is that it increases your sex life.
sentences.zh: 一些最新的研究表明，这之所以有效的原因之一是它增加了你们的性生活。

sentences.en: It makes your sex more lively.
sentences.zh: 它让你们的性生活更活跃。

sentences.en: So that's one big thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一大重点。

sentences.en: Another big thing is your sex life and just physical contact is really important.
sentences.zh: 另一个重点是你的性生活，仅仅是身体接触也非常重要。

sentences.en: You don't need to have sex every day.
sentences.zh: 你不需要每天都做爱。

sentences.en: You know, once an hour is, you don't need to have sex every day.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每小时一次是，你不需要每天都做爱。

sentences.en: In fact, once a week for most people is just about the right amount, you know, and it's important that both of you want to have it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，对大多数人来说，每周一次是恰到好处的，你知道，重要的是你们俩都想做。

sentences.en: You enjoy it and you have a little variation what you do a little bit.
sentences.zh: 你们享受它，并且在做的事情上有一点点变化。

sentences.en: But that's sort of crucial.
sentences.zh: 但这算是至关重要的。

sentences.en: But, you know, sometimes like in one in the big national sample we did of people who claim to be intensely in love after, you know, 10, 20 years together.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，有时像我们在全国性大样本中做的那样，有些人声称在在一起10年、20年后依然深爱着对方。

sentences.en: There were a few older couples who weren't ever having sex, but they had a lot of physical contact.
sentences.zh: 有几对年长的夫妇从来没有性生活，但他们有很多身体接触。

sentences.en: And in fact, even on a daily basis, aside from the sex, just, you know, holding your partner's hand, hugging them, those sorts of things,
sentences.zh: 事实上，即使在日常生活中，除了性之外，仅仅是，你知道，握住你伴侣的手，拥抱他们，这类事情，

sentences.en: to the extent it's legitimate and feels honest, is really important.
sentences.zh: 只要是真诚的且感觉真实，就非常重要。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of research showing that.
sentences.zh: 有很多研究都表明了这一点。

sentences.en: So, you know, physical contact, sex, and of course, eking time out together alone from your children or your extended family is kind of important in part to have sex, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，身体接触、性，当然，从孩子或大家庭中挤出时间独处，在某种程度上很重要，部分原因是为了过性生活，你知道。

sentences.en: So it's, but it sounds like you should be putting aside some time for sort of a date night and maybe, maybe go skydiving, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，但这听起来你应该留出一些时间来安排约会之夜，也许，也许去跳伞，你知道，

sentences.en: do something that's really going to get your blood pumping.
sentences.zh: 做一些真正能让你们热血沸腾的事情。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: Skydiving is a great example.
sentences.zh: 跳伞就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: It's important that you do things that are challenging and interesting, but not more than you can handle.
sentences.zh: 重要的是你要做一些具有挑战性和有趣的事情，但不要超过你能承受的范围。

sentences.en: There's, there's this study showing this sort of curvilinear effect that up to the point where you can handle the challenge, the more challenge, the better.
sentences.zh: 有研究显示这种曲线效应，即在你能承受挑战的范围内，挑战越大越好。

sentences.en: But when it goes beyond that.
sentences.zh: 但当它超过那个限度时。

sentences.en: Diminishing returns.
sentences.zh: 边际效应递减。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like my wife, you know, really loves, uh, uh, going out in the water and really loves whales.
sentences.zh: 就像我妻子，你知道，真的很喜欢，呃，呃，去水上，真的很喜欢鲸鱼。

sentences.en: And I love whales too.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢鲸鱼。

sentences.en: So she said, why don't we go on a whale watching trip?
sentences.zh: 所以她说，我们为什么不去参加观鲸之旅呢？

sentences.en: But I get seasick.
sentences.zh: 但我晕船。

sentences.en: And so we took all, I, we said, well, let's try.
sentences.zh: 所以我们带了所有，我，我们说，好吧，试试看。

sentences.en: And I took all these pills and things you put on your wrist and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 我吃了所有这些药，还有戴在手腕上的东西之类的。

sentences.en: And we went out and I fed the whales.
sentences.zh: 我们出海了，然后我喂了鲸鱼（指晕船呕吐）。

sentences.en: But she had a great time.
sentences.zh: 但她玩得很开心。

sentences.en: And she, well, yeah, she was supporting me and the support was good, you know, feeling her support.
sentences.zh: 而且她，嗯，是的，她在支持我，这种支持很好，你知道，感受到她的支持。

sentences.en: But, you know, we had to stay out there a long time because it was a group, you know, thing.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们必须在那待很长时间，因为这是一个团体活动。

sentences.en: But so it is important to do things.
sentences.zh: 所以做这些事情很重要。

sentences.en: They have to be new, as I say, taking a cooking class together or, or, you know, a dance class, of course, is some physical thing, but it's not the physical.
sentences.zh: 它们必须是新鲜的，正如我所说，一起上烹饪课，或者，或者，你知道，舞蹈课，当然，这是一种身体活动，但它不仅仅是身体上的。

sentences.en: You know, we've done studies when people initially meet and when they initially meet being physiologically turned on, I don't mean sexually, but just, you know, stirred up, um,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们做过研究，当人们最初见面时，当他们最初见面时，生理上的兴奋，我不是指性方面的，只是，你知道，被搅动了，嗯，

sentences.en: does make you more likely to be attracted to a new person.
sentences.zh: 确实会让你更有可能被一个新的人吸引。

sentences.en: And the novelty of it isn't what matters.
sentences.zh: 而且这种新鲜感本身并不重要。

sentences.en: But in a long-term relationship, what matters is the novelty and not the amount of physical stirring.
sentences.zh: 但在长期关系中，重要的是新鲜感，而不是生理上的那种悸动。

sentences.en: And if, when you meet a new person, if you've just, you know, exercised and, you know, worked up, you know, for 20 minutes and you're all stirred up, you're more likely,
sentences.zh: 如果你在遇见一个新人时，刚好，你知道，刚运动完，你知道，已经，你知道，锻炼了20分钟，整个人处于兴奋状态，那么你更有可能，

sentences.en: if they're reasonably attractive, you're more likely to think, oh, I know why I'm worked up.
sentences.zh: 如果对方长得还不错，你更有可能觉得，哦，我知道我为什么会心跳加速了。

sentences.en: I'm attracted to them.
sentences.zh: 是因为我被他们吸引了。

sentences.en: But in a long-term relationship, you know, you're used to being worked up from exercising.
sentences.zh: 但在长期关系中，你知道，你已经习惯了运动带来的那种生理兴奋。

sentences.en: It doesn't, it's the novelty that sort of rekindles things.
sentences.zh: 这没用，真正能重燃激情的，是新鲜感。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 没错，这很有道理。

sentences.en: And, and then there's some others that are important.
sentences.zh: 而且，还有其他一些重要因素。

sentences.en: And here's where the 36 questions come in.
sentences.zh: 这就是那36个问题发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: Deep friendships with other couples matter a lot.
sentences.zh: 与其他伴侣建立深厚的友谊非常重要。

sentences.en: Now, the 36 questions, for the few people who aren't familiar with it, is a procedure that takes about 45 minutes, um,
sentences.zh: 现在，对于那些不太了解的人来说，这36个问题是一套大约需要45分钟的流程，嗯，

sentences.en: that we designed so we could create closeness in the laboratory.
sentences.zh: 是我们为了在实验室里创造亲密感而设计的。

sentences.en: The problem is that if you want to study the effects of closeness scientifically, you want to be able to randomly assign people to be close or not.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，如果你想科学地研究亲密感的影响，你就需要能够随机分配人们是否亲密。

sentences.en: If you just take people who are close versus not, they have different histories, they chose each other.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是拿亲密和不亲密的人做对比，他们有不同的过往，是他们自己选择了彼此。

sentences.en: So we wanted to be able to create a, a procedure, which in 45 minutes could do that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想设计一套流程，能在45分钟内实现这一点。

sentences.en: And so we developed that procedure and that was not intended to make people fall in love, was to make people close.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开发了那套流程，它的初衷并不是为了让人坠入爱河，而是为了让人变得亲密。

sentences.en: In fact, most of the people in our studies were heterosexual people paired with same sex others, but it created closeness, created closeness.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们研究中的大多数人都是异性恋者与同性配对，但它确实创造了亲密感，创造了亲密感。

sentences.en: And that was the idea.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的初衷。

sentences.en: Now, of course, if everything else is in place and closeness can add to the chance of falling in love initially, but that wasn't the goal.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果其他条件都具备，亲密感确实能增加最初坠入爱河的机会，但这并非我们的目标。

sentences.en: Now, what does it do?
sentences.zh: 那么，它有什么作用呢？

sentences.en: Well, if you do it with an ongoing partner, it does, you know, it does make you feel closer to your partner if you're in a long-term relationship,
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你和现任伴侣一起做，它确实，你知道，如果你处于长期关系中，它确实会让你感觉和伴侣更亲近，

sentences.en: but it doesn't particularly increase love.
sentences.zh: 但它并不会特别增加爱意。

sentences.en: But there's all this research showing that if couples have a close friendship with another couple, they're more likely to be in love and happy in their relationship.
sentences.zh: 但有大量研究表明，如果伴侣之间与其他伴侣有深厚的友谊，他们更有可能相爱，并在关系中感到幸福。

sentences.en: We don't know which is causing which.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道究竟是谁导致了谁。

sentences.en: The initial study was done by Rich Slatcher.
sentences.zh: 最初的研究是由Rich Slatcher完成的。

sentences.en: This was his dissertation, in fact, and then later I collaborated with him on a bunch of studies and Keith Welker, another former student of his.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是他的博士论文，后来我和他以及他的另一位前学生Keith Welker合作进行了一系列研究。

sentences.en: And what we found was that when a couple does it by themselves, as I say, they get closer, but it doesn't necessarily increase their love.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当一对伴侣独自做这件事时，正如我所说，他们会变得更亲近，但这并不一定会增加他们的爱意。

sentences.en: But when two couples do it together as a foursome, each of the four answers each of the 36 questions.
sentences.zh: 但当两对伴侣一起做，四个人在一起时，每个人都要回答这36个问题。

sentences.en: It not only makes them closer to each other and to the other couple, but it increases their passionate love within the couple.
sentences.zh: 这不仅让他们彼此之间以及与另一对伴侣之间更亲近，还能增加伴侣内部的激情之爱。

sentences.en: And they're really great questions.
sentences.zh: 而且这些问题真的很棒。

sentences.en: I mean, can you just toss a couple out there?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你能随便抛出几个问题吗？

sentences.en: Because I know you start at a certain level of, you know, sort of familiar and then you go deep.
sentences.zh: 因为我知道你们是从某种，你知道，比较熟悉的程度开始，然后逐渐深入。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The idea of this came from survey research showing that when people form friendships, which is our main focus at the time, they do so by initially not being, you know,
sentences.zh: 这个想法源于调查研究，研究显示当人们建立友谊时——这是我们当时的主要关注点——他们最初并不是，你知道，

sentences.en: sort of exchanging and then gradually revealing more and more.
sentences.zh: 那种交换信息，然后逐渐透露更多。

sentences.en: You know, if someone reveals too much too fast, it sort of is a little scary.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果有人透露得太多太快，会让人有点害怕。

sentences.en: It puts you off and, you know.
sentences.zh: 这会让你退缩，你知道的。

sentences.en: So we set up a set of questions where initially you answer questions, you know, if you could, you know, go out with to dinner with anyone in history,
sentences.zh: 所以我们设定了一组问题，最初你回答的问题是，比如，如果你可以，你知道，和历史上任何人共进晚餐，

sentences.en: who would you want to go out to dinner with and things like that.
sentences.zh: 你想和谁共进晚餐，诸如此类的问题。

sentences.en: And then towards the end, you know, we initially were doing this with college age students.
sentences.zh: 然后到最后，你知道，我们最初是针对大学生进行这项研究的。

sentences.en: You know, how would you feel if your mother died?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你的母亲去世了，你会作何感想？

sentences.en: You know, I mean, it's, you know, it's so it moves along.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，它，你知道，它是循序渐进的。

sentences.en: And we also threw in two or three other questions that mattered.
sentences.zh: 我们还加入了两三个其他重要的问题。

sentences.en: After a little while, we asked, have you noticed anything you have in common with the other person?
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，我们问，你有没有注意到你和对方有什么共同点？

sentences.en: And we never say, have you noticed anything you don't have in common?
sentences.zh: 我们从不说，你有没有注意到你们有什么不同之处？

sentences.en: Again, being in common isn't that important, but thinking you're in common.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，有共同点并不重要，重要的是认为你们有共同点。

sentences.en: And then also a little later, we have some items that say, name some things you like about.
sentences.zh: 然后过一会儿，我们有一些条目是说，列举一些你喜欢的，

sentences.en: You've noticed you like about the other person.
sentences.zh: 你注意到你喜欢对方的哪些方面。

sentences.en: Turns out that's a huge factor in feeling close to someone.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这是让人感到亲近的一个重要因素。

sentences.en: And in fact, it's a huge factor in initially falling in love is thinking the other person likes you.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这也是最初坠入爱河的一个重要因素，那就是认为对方也喜欢你。

sentences.en: Now, you know, people think 36 questions, how long is that going to take?
sentences.zh: 现在，你知道，人们会想36个问题，那要花多长时间？

sentences.en: There's three sets of 12 questions.
sentences.zh: 总共有三组，每组12个问题。

sentences.en: And we say, don't rush it.
sentences.zh: 我们说，别着急。

sentences.en: We don't expect you to get through all of them.
sentences.zh: 我们并不指望你们能全部答完。

sentences.en: And the reason we have 12 questions is some people move quickly.
sentences.zh: 我们设置12个问题的原因是有些人进展很快。

sentences.en: We don't want them to run out, but most people will get through six or seven.
sentences.zh: 我们不想让他们没题可答，但大多数人会完成六七个。

sentences.en: And you do this with another couple.
sentences.zh: 而且你是和另一对伴侣一起做。

sentences.en: You can do it as long as you want, but it's better not to take too long.
sentences.zh: 你们想做多久都可以，但最好不要花太长时间。

sentences.en: You know, you'll get bored with it, but it's it's really valuable.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你会觉得无聊，但它真的很有价值。

sentences.en: And in fact, my wife and I have done this once or twice with couples.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我和我妻子曾和几对伴侣做过一两次。

sentences.en: We know a little bit by Zoom.
sentences.zh: 我们通过Zoom了解了一些。

sentences.en: It's something you can do over the, you know, by Zoom with another couple who's on the other side of the world, like some friends we have in Sweden.
sentences.zh: 这是你可以通过Zoom和另一对远在世界另一端的伴侣一起做的事情，比如我们在瑞典的一些朋友。

sentences.en: So it's it's a pretty powerful thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是一件非常有力量的事情。

sentences.en: One thing I should remind people about the 36 questions, if they're using them either initially to get close or with a friend or, you know, someone they're dating,
sentences.zh: 关于这36个问题，我应该提醒大家一点，如果他们是在最初为了建立亲密感而使用，或者和朋友，或者，你知道，约会对象一起使用，

sentences.en: is you can't use the same set of questions again and again and again because you get you know the answers.
sentences.zh: 就是你不能一遍又一遍地使用同一套问题，因为你已经，你知道答案了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, you know, this episode is being timed to mark Valentine's Day.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，这一集的时间安排是为了纪念情人节。

sentences.en: And I'm just wondering, you know, a lot of people kind of poo poo the importance of a hallmark holiday in a long term relationship.
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，你知道，很多人对长期关系中这种商业化的节日不屑一顾。

sentences.en: Do you think that a day set aside to recognize and celebrate romantic love helps relationships?
sentences.zh: 你认为专门留出一天来认可和庆祝浪漫爱情对关系有帮助吗？

sentences.en: Or is it something that just leads to unmet expectations and, you know, an overpriced restaurant meal?
sentences.zh: 还是说这只会导致期望落空，以及，你知道，一顿价格过高的餐厅晚餐？

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know of any research on this, but I think putting your attention on the relationship is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不知道这方面的研究，但我认为把注意力放在关系上是一件好事。

sentences.en: There's a couple more things you can do to sparkle it up.
sentences.zh: 还有几件事可以让你增添火花。

sentences.en: And one of them is to express gratitude and to think about what you're grateful for in your relationship.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是表达感激，并思考你在关系中感激什么。

sentences.en: And a holiday is a good day to do that.
sentences.zh: 而节日是一个做这件事的好日子。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: What am I grateful for that my partner has given me?
sentences.zh: 伴侣给了我什么，我对此心存感激？

sentences.en: And of course, it's also important on a day to day basis when something happens.
sentences.zh: 当然，在日常生活中，当某事发生时，这也是很重要的。

sentences.en: You know, again, you want to be honest about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，同样，你要真诚地表达。

sentences.en: You don't want to say thank you for something.
sentences.zh: 你不想为了某事而说谢谢。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 那不重要。

sentences.en: And one thing that's interesting from some of the recent research,
sentences.zh: 最近的一些研究中有一点很有趣，

sentences.en: it especially matters in a long term relationship when you're saying you appreciate they did that thing to not only let them know how hard you thought they worked to make it happen,
sentences.zh: 在长期关系中，当你表达对他们所做之事的感激时，不仅要让他们知道你认为他们为了实现这件事付出了多少努力，这一点尤为重要，

sentences.en: but how much it meant to you, how much you got from they're doing it.
sentences.zh: 还要让他们知道这对你意味着什么，你从他们的行为中获得了多少。

sentences.en: So expressing gratitude and feeling gratitude is really important.
sentences.zh: 所以表达感激和感受感激真的很重要。

sentences.en: And it also reminds me, there's one other thing I didn't get to, some wonderful work on celebrating your partner's successes.
sentences.zh: 这也提醒了我，还有一件事我没提到，就是关于庆祝伴侣成功的一些精彩研究。

sentences.en: You know, if your partner has something good happen, you know, don't just say, oh, that's nice.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你的伴侣发生了什么好事，你知道，不要只说，哦，那很好。

sentences.en: You know, let them know, really let them know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，让他们知道，真正地让他们知道。

sentences.en: It turns out that matters more than supporting them when things go badly.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这比在事情进展不顺时支持他们更重要。

sentences.en: My wife does this research on the highly sensitive person.
sentences.zh: 我妻子在做关于高敏感人群的研究。

sentences.en: We collaborate, which is one of the exciting things we do together.
sentences.zh: 我们合作，这是我们一起做的令人兴奋的事情之一。

sentences.en: And, you know, we've also collaborated on the relationship research.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们也合作过关系研究。

sentences.en: But she submitted a little while back, she submitted a paper, review paper to a very top journal, psychology journal on the state of the research on highly sensitive people.
sentences.zh: 但她不久前提交了一篇论文，一篇综述论文，投给了一家非常顶级的期刊，心理学期刊，关于高敏感人群的研究现状。

sentences.en: And it was a very top journal.
sentences.zh: 那是一本非常顶级的期刊。

sentences.en: We thought the chances of it being accepted were not that high.
sentences.zh: 我们认为被录用的几率并不高。

sentences.en: I was a co-author, but it was her work.
sentences.zh: 我是合著者，但那是她的工作。

sentences.en: I was home when the email came in saying the editor loved it, the reviewers loved it.
sentences.zh: 当邮件发来时我在家，说编辑很喜欢，审稿人也很喜欢。

sentences.en: And so I made a poster of that and put it on the wall for when she came home.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了一张海报贴在墙上，等她回家时看。

sentences.en: We had a great night.
sentences.zh: 我们度过了一个很棒的夜晚。

sentences.en: But celebrating your partner's successes also matters.
sentences.zh: 但庆祝伴侣的成功也很重要。

sentences.en: And I suppose you could make a point of that to some extent on like, hey, we're still together.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以在某种程度上强调这一点，比如，嘿，我们还在一起。

sentences.en: That's a kind of success.
sentences.zh: 那也是一种成功。

sentences.en: So some of the relationship stressors that we've talked about, boredom and, you know, just tension have been really, really abundant in our lives these last two years.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈到的一些关系压力源，无聊和，你知道，仅仅是紧张，在过去两年的生活中确实非常非常多。

sentences.en: And it may be a little soon to be talking about what we know about what the pandemic is doing to people's relationships.
sentences.zh: 现在谈论我们对疫情如何影响人们的关系了解多少可能还为时过早。

sentences.en: But I'm just wondering, have you thought about this?
sentences.zh: 但我只是在想，你考虑过这个问题吗？

sentences.en: Are you doing any research in this area?
sentences.zh: 你在这个领域做研究吗？

sentences.en: What are you seeing?
sentences.zh: 你看到了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I haven't myself done any research in this area.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我自己没有在这个领域做过研究。

sentences.en: Several of my collaborators, colleagues have.
sentences.zh: 我的几位合作者、同事做过。

sentences.en: Rich Slatcher, who actually was on one of these podcasts, has done a lot of work in that.
sentences.zh: Rich Slatcher，他实际上参加过这些播客中的一个，在这方面做了很多工作。

sentences.en: Rhonda Belzerini, a former graduate student of mine, has done a lot of work in this area.
sentences.zh: Rhonda Belzerini，我的一位前研究生，在这个领域做了很多工作。

sentences.en: But they're still just starting to get their results.
sentences.zh: 但他们才刚刚开始得到结果。

sentences.en: And I haven't been following it as closely as I might.
sentences.zh: 我也没有像我应该做的那样密切关注它。

sentences.en: So I can't really comment on that.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的无法对此发表评论。

sentences.en: But, you know, I mean, I think the one or two things that follow from my research is that, again, even though you can't do the usual things or even the usual novel things,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我的意思是，我认为从我的研究中得出的一两件事是，再说一次，即使你不能做通常的事情，甚至不能做通常的新鲜事，

sentences.en: look for things you can do.
sentences.zh: 寻找你能做的事情。

sentences.en: Like I mentioned doing the 36 questions with another couple on the other side of the world by Zoom.
sentences.zh: 就像我提到的通过Zoom和远在世界另一端的另一对伴侣做那36个问题。

sentences.en: You can take a dancing class by Zoom, you know, or, you know, things you can do, you know, sit together and cook some food you've never done together if you can,
sentences.zh: 你可以通过Zoom上舞蹈课，你知道，或者，你知道，你们可以一起做的事情，你知道，坐在一起做一些你们从未一起做过的食物，如果可以的话，

sentences.en: if that's interesting to you, you know.
sentences.zh: 如果这对你们来说很有趣，你知道。

sentences.en: And also, you do need some time for yourself.
sentences.zh: 而且，你也确实需要一些属于自己的时间。

sentences.en: And it's important that people, if they're just alone as a couple, also have a little time alone so that they're not feeling overburdened.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，如果人们只是作为伴侣单独在一起，也要有一点独处的时间，这样他们就不会感到负担过重。

sentences.en: Are there signs that the relationship can't really be salvaged?
sentences.zh: 有没有迹象表明这段关系真的无法挽救了？

sentences.en: I mean, sometimes, you know, you reach a rocky point, but even the research that you have done and the suggestions that you make to bring people together,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有时，你知道，你会到达一个困难的阶段，但即使是你所做的研究和你提出的让人们走到一起的建议，

sentences.en: are there some relationships where it really just doesn't matter?
sentences.zh: 是否有些关系真的无所谓了？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: It's tough.
sentences.zh: 这很难。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, if you're being physically abused by someone, a partner, you know, in those kind of cases, or if you've got a partner who's, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然，如果你受到某人，伴侣的身体虐待，你知道，在那种情况下，或者如果你有一个伴侣，你知道，

sentences.en: an alcoholic and can't stop and something like that, that can be tough.
sentences.zh: 是个酒鬼，无法停止，诸如此类的事情，那可能会很困难。

sentences.en: Short of that, it seems like if people pull these things, you know, can pull these things together to some extent, they can make almost any relationship work.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，似乎如果人们能把这些事情，你知道，能在一定程度上把这些事情处理好，他们几乎可以让任何关系奏效。

sentences.en: So, if you're really sincere in your effort, I mean, you have to take it seriously and try to follow the instructions.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你真的真诚地努力，我的意思是，你必须认真对待并尝试遵循说明。

sentences.en: I mean, I've read a fair amount of John Gottman, for example, and he does have a lot of things that he recommends that couples do together.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我读过不少John Gottman的书，例如，他确实有很多建议伴侣一起做的事情。

sentences.en: And they, at least as far as his work goes, he says they work.
sentences.zh: 而且，至少就他的工作而言，他说这些方法有效。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, you need both of the members of the couple to be willing to do something.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你需要伴侣双方都愿意做些什么。

sentences.en: And of course, as I say, sometimes it's just yourself.
sentences.zh: 当然，正如我所说，有时只是你自己。

sentences.en: Sometimes just getting your own therapy or doing something to make yourself better off will make the relationship better and also give you more freedom to do things to make the relationship better.
sentences.zh: 有时仅仅是接受你自己的治疗或做些事情让自己变得更好，就会让关系变得更好，也会给你更多的自由去做些事情让关系变得更好。

sentences.en: So, you've been studying relationships now for, I don't know, 50 years, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，你研究关系已经，我不知道，50年了，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's a long time that you've been working in this area.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你在这个领域工作了很长时间。

sentences.en: What are the big questions that you still want to answer?
sentences.zh: 你仍然想回答的重大问题是什么？

sentences.en: We still, you know, we know that these things I went through, each of them predicts more love, more satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然，你知道，我们知道我经历的这些事情，每一项都预示着更多的爱，更多的满足感。

sentences.en: But we don't know for sure, you know, we know a little bit from the survey, what things really make the few couples that are at the very top get there.
sentences.zh: 但我们并不确定，你知道，我们从调查中了解了一点，什么事情真正让那极少数处于顶端的伴侣达到了那个位置。

sentences.en: And so, I'm now doing some research with Terry Orbach and Rosie Shrout, who has this great data set.
sentences.zh: 所以，我现在正在和Terry Orbach以及Rosie Shrout进行一些研究，她有这个很棒的数据集。

sentences.en: And also, we're trying to gather some other data set of people who've done longitudinal research.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们正在尝试收集其他做过纵向研究的人的数据集。

sentences.en: And we're trying to see what, from early on, predicts which couples are not only happy, which is what most of it's been done, but which are super happy, which are, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们试图看看，从早期开始，什么能预测哪些伴侣不仅幸福——这是大多数研究已经做过的——而且是超级幸福，也就是，你知道，

sentences.en: very intensely in love.
sentences.zh: 非常热烈地相爱。

sentences.en: And so, we're trying to sort out those data.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们正在尝试整理这些数据。

sentences.en: So, it's not like we're not collecting new data.
sentences.zh: 所以，并不是我们没有在收集新数据。

sentences.en: We're trying to sort that out and try to get a strong handle on it.
sentences.zh: 我们正在尝试整理这些，并试图很好地掌握它。

sentences.en: You know, we presume it's a lot of these factors, but we don't know for sure.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们推测这是很多这些因素的结果，但我们并不确定。

sentences.en: I mean, we're pretty sure, but it may be just particular combinations that really make it happen or something we haven't looked at.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们很确定，但这可能只是特定的组合真正促成了它，或者是一些我们还没有看过的东西。

sentences.en: Well, I will look forward to seeing that.
sentences.zh: 好的，我很期待看到那一天的到来。

sentences.en: I appreciate you taking the time to talk to us today, Dr. Aaron.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天抽出时间接受我们的采访，亚伦博士。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you for inviting me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们的邀请。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be able to share so much of what our field knows.
sentences.zh: 能分享我们领域所掌握的这么多知识，我感到非常荣幸。
